definition: In natural language processing, open information extraction (OIE) is the task of generating a structured, machine-readable representation of the information in text, usually in the form of triples or n-ary propositions..
details: In natural language processing, open information extraction (OIE) is the task of generating a structured, machine-readable representation of the information in text, usually in the form of triples or n-ary propositions.

explainer.lead: Open information extraction turns text into structured, machine-readable information. It matters because it captures relations without a predefined target schema.

tiers.eli5: It is like turning sentences into simple fact lists a computer can read, like 'Paris — is capital of — France'.
tiers.practitioner: The usual output is triples or n-ary propositions.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as generating a structured, machine-readable representation of the information in text, usually as triples or n-ary propositions. No further limits are given.

explainer.example: A sentence about a company and its headquarters is output as a triple linking the two.
